body: Are you defining port when using the unix_socket?

On properly configured server, this works -

```
$dsn = "pgsql:dbname={$config['database']}";
```

So didn't really need to define the port

Did you configure your database with a config array or a DSN URL?
When using this config array, everything seems to work as expected on my end:

``` php
$config = [
    'persistent' => false,
    'host' => '',
    'database' => 'cake',
    'username' => 'user',
    'password' => 'pass',
    'port' => 5432,
    'flags' => [1 => true, 2 => false],
    'encoding' => 'a-language',
    'timezone' => 'Antartica',
    'schema' => 'fooblic',
    'unix_socket' => true,
    'init' => ['Execute this', 'this too']
];
```
Thanks for the additional information @1worldtech-bhoffman I can take a look at how we could prioritize the unix_socket mode other host/port.

issue.title: Fix postgres not supporting unix_socket.

repository.name: cakephp
repository.description: CakePHP: The Rapid Development Framework for PHP - Official Repository

issue.body:
While it was documented as working, it totally didn't work.

Refs #6368

body:
@markstory I believe I led us to an incorrect/inconsistent solution.  
According to the docs the solution implemented will work:  http://www.postgresql.org/docs/8.3/static/libpq-connect.html
"Without either a host name or host address, libpq will connect using a local Unix-domain socket; or on machines without Unix-domain sockets, it will attempt to connect to localhost."

However when using plugins or 3rd party libraries such as Migrations Plugin we discovered that the solution implemented causes issues as phinx handles the connection to postgres similar to CakePHP did prior to the fix.  

I think the correct fix is a matter of proper documentation and proper permissions to the database server.
I found this page helpful in correcting the issue in our environments: https://help.ubuntu.com/community/PostgreSQL

Using a DSN similar to this:  `" psql "host=/tmp port=5433 user=bob ..."` where the socket directory is specified in the host value works properly for common usage of PDO_PGSQL DSN (i.e. phinx https://github.com/robmorgan/phinx/blob/0.4.x-dev/src/Phinx/Db/Adapter/PostgresAdapter.php#L62)

The issue with using the unix_socket_directories is that you need heightened permissions on the database server to run the following command to discover where the socket directory resides 
`sudo -u postgres psql -c "SHOW unix_socket_directories;"`  i.e. in our case the socket directory was /var/run/postgresql

In summary I think the docs should provide details on how to create the DB connection and point developers in the right direction to the documentation needed to create the proper connection to the unix socket.

a sample app.php datasource

```
    'Datasources' => [
        'default' => [
            'className' => 'Cake\Database\Connection',
            'driver' => 'Cake\Database\Driver\Postgres',
            'persistent' => false, 
            'host' => '/var/run/postgresql',    // in pdo it will use unix socket
            'username' => 'user',
            'password' => 'password',
            'database' => 'db_name',
            'encoding' => 'utf8',
            'timezone' => 'UTC',
            'cacheMetadata' => true,
            'quoteIdentifiers' => false,
        ],
```

I don't know much about postgres to be honest, especially not the unixsocket approach, as I generally always just use TCP connections. It sounds like you know more though, perhaps you could do a pull request to update the documentation?
@markstory I will attempt to help update the docs sometime this week.
